### 2. Architectural Scaffolding

Large structural changes that enable future work rather than deliver end-user value directly.

**A. Horizontally scalable producer / ingester / event bus split (v0.0.44 "major architectural overhaul")**

The [`producer/`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/producer) module introduces:

- A `Scheduler` + `Processor` separation (separate files)
- Asynq task queue for monitor dispatch

The [`ingester/`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/ingester) module consumes those tasks and separates the worker tier from the scheduling tier.

The [`infra/redis_event_bus.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/infra/redis_event_bus.go) is a Redis Pub/Sub implementation of the [`EventBus`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/modules/events/event.go?L38-47) interface, enabling cross-node event propagation. This is explicitly a breaking infrastructure change (CHANGELOG `0.0.44`, PR #207).

**B. Dual repository pattern (SQL + Mongo) for all entities**

Every domain module has a parallel `.sql.repository.go` and `.mongo.repository.go` (e.g., [`monitor.sql.repository.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/modules/monitor/monitor.sql.repository.go), `monitor.mongo.repository.go`). This is scaffolding for multi-database support, not a user feature. The SQL repositories use `uptrace/bun` with a separate `sqlModel` struct and two-way mapping functions (`toDomainModelFromSQL`, `toSQLModel`) to preserve a clean domain layer.

**C. Dependency injection via `go.uber.org/dig`**

Every module has a `*.dig.go` file wiring constructors into the DI container. This is architectural scaffolding — it is invisible to users but required for the modular structure. Example: [`producer.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/producer), [`api_key.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/api_key).

[`server.go:107`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/server.go?L107): `// server.Use(LogMiddleware(logger))` — disabled middleware.

### 8. Boilerplate

Structural repetition required by the architecture but carrying no unique logic.

**A. `*.dig.go` DI wiring files**

One per module (31 modules × 1 file each). Each is a thin wrapper around `dig.Provide(...)` or `dig.Supply(...)`. No logic, just registration. Examples: [`api_key.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/api_key), [`producer.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/producer).

**B. Mongo vs. SQL repository pairs**

The `*.mongo.repository.go` and `*.sql.repository.go` for each entity repeat the same CRUD interface with different storage backends. The SQL variant adds a `sqlModel` adapter struct and two mapping functions; the Mongo variant uses BSON tags. Once the first was written the remaining are structural copies. This is boilerplate by the taxonomy definition — necessary but non-novel.

**C. Notification provider files**

24 files in [`providers/`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/notification_channel/providers) all follow the same shape (config struct, `Send(ctx, payload)` function). The first integration is a feature; subsequent ones are largely boilerplate filling out the provider interface. **Ambiguity note**: the line between "feature" and "boilerplate" blurs here — each provider has business-specific API integration details, so labeling later providers pure boilerplate would undercount their novelty.

---

### 9. Dependency Migration

No evidence of a migration away from one dependency to another at this revision. The `go.mod` shows a wide and stable dependency surface (bun 1.2.14, gin 1.10.0, asynq 0.25.1, socket.io v2, etc.). All major library choices appear already settled. **Mark as absent at this revision.**

---

## Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

One task shape present in the codebase does not map cleanly onto the given categories:

**"Integration slice"** — the addition of a new monitor type or notification provider follows a strict pattern: config struct → validator → executor/sender implementation → registry registration → optional test. It is more than a feature (it requires fulfilling a formal interface contract) but less than architectural scaffolding (no structural change to the system). Within the existing taxonomy this is correctly classified as **feature**, but the regularity of the pattern suggests it could usefully be tracked as a sub-type: **`feature/integration-slice`**. This would allow distinguishing pioneering features (e.g., the initial HTTP executor, the event bus) from routine protocol additions (SNMP, MQTT, RabbitMQ) that follow a template.

### 2. Architectural Scaffolding

Large structural changes that enable future work rather than deliver end-user value directly.

**A. Horizontally scalable producer / ingester / event bus split (v0.0.44 "major architectural overhaul")**

The [`producer/`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/producer) module introduces:
- Redis-based leader election (`leader_election.go`, [`LeaderElection`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/modules/producer/leader_election.go)) — only one producer node schedules checks at a time
- A `Scheduler` + `Processor` separation (separate files)
- Asynq task queue for monitor dispatch

The [`ingester/`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/ingester) module consumes those tasks and separates the worker tier from the scheduling tier.

The [`infra/redis_event_bus.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/infra/redis_event_bus.go) is a Redis Pub/Sub implementation of the [`EventBus`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/modules/events/event.go?L38-47) interface, enabling cross-node event propagation. This is explicitly a breaking infrastructure change (CHANGELOG `0.0.44`, PR #207).

**B. Dual repository pattern (SQL + Mongo) for all entities**

Every domain module has a parallel `.sql.repository.go` and `.mongo.repository.go` (e.g., [`monitor.sql.repository.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/blob/apps/server/internal/modules/monitor/monitor.sql.repository.go), `monitor.mongo.repository.go`). This is scaffolding for multi-database support, not a user feature. The SQL repositories use `uptrace/bun` with a separate `sqlModel` struct and two-way mapping functions (`toDomainModelFromSQL`, `toSQLModel`) to preserve a clean domain layer.

**C. Dependency injection via `go.uber.org/dig`**

Every module has a `*.dig.go` file wiring constructors into the DI container. This is architectural scaffolding — it is invisible to users but required for the modular structure. Example: [`producer.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/producer), [`api_key.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/api_key).

### 8. Boilerplate

Structural repetition required by the architecture but carrying no unique logic.

**A. `*.dig.go` DI wiring files**

One per module (31 modules × 1 file each). Each is a thin wrapper around `dig.Provide(...)` or `dig.Supply(...)`. No logic, just registration. Examples: [`api_key.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/api_key), [`producer.dig.go`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/producer).

**B. Mongo vs. SQL repository pairs**

The `*.mongo.repository.go` and `*.sql.repository.go` for each entity repeat the same CRUD interface with different storage backends. The SQL variant adds a `sqlModel` adapter struct and two mapping functions; the Mongo variant uses BSON tags. Once the first was written the remaining are structural copies. This is boilerplate by the taxonomy definition — necessary but non-novel.

**C. Notification provider files**

24 files in [`providers/`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/0xfurai-peekaping@742a60d94fdaacc977c09444b651f7cf1c1aab9e/-/tree/apps/server/internal/modules/notification_channel/providers) all follow the same shape (config struct, `Send(ctx, payload)` function). The first integration is a feature; subsequent ones are largely boilerplate filling out the provider interface. **Ambiguity note**: the line between "feature" and "boilerplate" blurs here — each provider has business-specific API integration details, so labeling later providers pure boilerplate would undercount their novelty.

---

### 9. Dependency Migration

No evidence of a migration away from one dependency to another at this revision. The `go.mod` shows a wide and stable dependency surface (bun 1.2.14, gin 1.10.0, asynq 0.25.1, socket.io v2, etc.). All major library choices appear already settled. **Mark as absent at this revision.**

---

## Taxonomy Refinement Proposal

One task shape present in the codebase does not map cleanly onto the given categories:

**"Integration slice"** — the addition of a new monitor type or notification provider follows a strict pattern: config struct → validator → executor/sender implementation → registry registration → optional test. It is more than a feature (it requires fulfilling a formal interface contract) but less than architectural scaffolding (no structural change to the system). Within the existing taxonomy this is correctly classified as **feature**, but the regularity of the pattern suggests it could usefully be tracked as a sub-type: **`feature/integration-slice`**. This would allow distinguishing pioneering features (e.g., the initial HTTP executor, the event bus) from routine protocol additions (SNMP, MQTT, RabbitMQ) that follow a template.
